evidence.note: Consistently reports per-shape correctness (pass_frac=1.0 / max_diff per shape) AND flags the binding worst-case shape: 'All 10 grader shapes pass correctness... shape 9 takes 925ms far exceeding 10.4ms.' Identifies N=2048 as the latency bottleneck early and keeps it as the reference target.

Catches cross-case regressions where a speed win breaks a correctness corner: FP16 overflows/NaN on Cauchy but not normal; BF16 fast but fails tolerance; TF32 bmm 0.11>0.02 while Triton tl.dot passes at 0.006. Explicitly reasons about which distribution/precision combo fails vs passes.

Maintains an explicit ledger: 'All 10 shapes pass (fraction 1.0), max diff 0.002-0.015, latency 564ms for N=2048 vs 10.4ms target' — tracks both axes simultaneously and notes shapes 3 & 5 have tiny failing fractions while others pass.

Repeatedly re-discovers the SAME dead-ends (FP16 overflow, 17ms .contiguous() cost, TF32 precision loss, grid-overhead) across ~30 rewrites without recognizing the circular pattern — the stuck-state detection anchor-10 requires is absent.

Final status is honest and accurate: passes all 10 shapes at max_diff 0.0 but latency 133ms misses the 10.4ms gate; correctly reports it did not meet the latency budget rather than falsely declaring success.

reasoning: The agent sustains an explicit, accurate ledger of correctness across shapes and distributions, consistently identifies the binding worst-case shape (N=2048), tracks each candidate against the 10400μs gate, and repeatedly catches cross-case regressions where a speed optimization (FP16/BF16/TF32) breaks a correctness corner (Cauchy overflow, tolerance failures) — squarely matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because it never detects its own circular state: it re-discovers the same falsified dead-ends (FP16 overflow, contiguous-copy cost, TF32 precision) across dozens of rewrites and keeps churning rather than recognizing the loop and reallocating effort.
